budget.honest: Algebra is already applied. This lane does not move the 18.28 ms routed-expert number. Still ~2.285x over the 8 ms budget.

numeric_equivalence_gate.statement: Reassociating L@(R@x) versus (L@R)@x changes f32 add order. Kernels are graded against the two-stage artifact oracle at tolerance 2e-5. Reconstruct-vs-two-stage drift is reported and is NOT a fail.

correctness.oracle: packed two-stage / fused rice artifact, never BF16 parent, never dense (L@R)@x

doctrine: REPRESENTATION -> ALGEBRA. Never reconstruct a structured representation when the algebra can consume it directly.

additive_codebooks.note: No PQ / additive-codebook organ is in the mixed-1p5 recipe.

down_proj.forbidden_path_absent: packed -> dense (2048 x 512) W -> W @ x is not implemented on the token path. decode_hgravs01_dense_f32_for_parity is CPU parity only (activation_weighted_svd.rs:677).

metal_fused_single_dispatch.quote: Fused y = L @ (R @ x) in one dispatch. Each threadgroup recomputes mid[rank]
metal_fused_single_dispatch.status: EXISTS but REJECTED as token path: sibling receipt fusion_negative, 5-13x slower because every TG recomputes R[160x512]. Metal has no grid-wide barrier.

gate_proj.algebra_question: not applicable; there is no low-rank / codebook / residual factor to consume

nonexpert_hgravu01.algebra_question: decode-in-register vs reconstruct; no U@(V@x) available. Shared expert is 8-bit, not hgravs01.
nonexpert_hgravu01.covers: embed, lm_head, attention, DeltaNet, norms, router, shared expert

metal_fused.quote: Binary simd + CSR residual in the same dispatch. Residual add order is serial on lane 0 after the binary reduction.

up_proj.not_reconstruct: Residual is a sparse correction fused into y, not applied to a dense reconstructed W.

down_proj.note: Shipped path already pays only factored_macs. Reconstruct-then-multiply would pay form_w + dense_w_x every token unless W were cached — and a decoded-W cache is already rejected (12 MiB/expert, 288 GiB if every layer-expert is cached).

up_proj.note: Fusing the 2% residual does not reduce FLOPs versus (B+R)@x. It eliminates the dense W temporary and the write of B+R.

next_bottleneck.label: DIRTY_ENGINEERING
next_bottleneck.what: up_proj binary decode / occupancy, ~17.25 us, ~45% of the remaining 38 us per expert. Achieved ~15 GB/s. Still decode/occupancy bound, not DRAM bound, not reconstruct-W bound.

temporaries.zero_temporary_principle: mid[160] f32 is the only down_proj temporary. No (2048 x 512) W. up residual uses bind-time expanded indices, not dense W.

timing.label: DIRTY_ENGINEERING

down.note: both arms already L@(R@x). Serial two-dispatch vs simd3 two-dispatch. Not reconstruct vs factors.

gate.note: occupancy, not algebra. Already decode-in-register both arms.

up.note: both arms already fuse residual into y. Occupancy, not reconstruct-vs-fuse.

timing.why_no_new_gpu: Algebra question is already answered in shipped kernels. A reconstruct-then-multiply Metal arm is forbidden (faster-by-reconstructing is rejected; never materialize dense W). Re-timing the already-factored kernels would only restate the occupancy lane.

verdict: The shipped Q80 down_proj token path already executes y = L @ (R @ x). It does not reconstruct dense W. Implementing a reconstruct-then-multiply kernel would be a regression against the standing law and is refused. This lane is a confirmed negative, not a kernel rewrite.
